ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the circuit there is a 20 V ideal voltage source, and beside it there is a 20 kΩ resistor connected in parallel with this voltage source. The upper left is connected through a 5 kΩ resistor to the P terminal of a single-pole double-throw switch; the switch switches from P to Q at t=0. The Q terminal is connected through a vertical wire to the bottom common node. The right side of the switch is connected through another 5 kΩ resistor to the right-side node. This right-side node has a 1 mF capacitor connected in parallel to ground, and the capacitor voltage v(t) is marked as positive on top and negative on bottom; at the same time there is also a branch in which a 10 kΩ resistor and a 0.1 mH inductor are connected in series and then connected to the bottom common node. Reasoning: When t<0, the switch has been at P for a long time, and the circuit is in DC steady state. In DC steady state, the capacitor is open-circuited and the inductor is short-circuited. The 20 kΩ resistor is only connected in parallel with the ideal 20 V source and does not change the voltage of the upper node of the power source. The right-side node is obtained by voltage division through the series path 5 kΩ + 5 kΩ + 10 kΩ: the total resistance is 20 kΩ, and the current is 20 V / 20 kΩ = 1 mA. Therefore the voltage of the right-side node, namely the voltage on the 10 kΩ, is v(0-) = 1 mA × 10 kΩ = 10 V; the inductor branch current i_L(0-) = 1 mA, with direction downward. Since the capacitor voltage is continuous and the inductor current is continuous, v(0+) = 10 V, i_L(0+) = 1 mA downward. After t=0, the switch is connected to Q, and the left end of the right-side 5 kΩ resistor is grounded. Write KCL for the node at the top end of the capacitor at t=0+, taking the current flowing from the node to ground as positive: C dv/dt + v/5 kΩ + i_L = 0. Substitute C = 1 mF = 0.001 F, v = 10 V, i_L = 0.001 A: 0.001 dv/dt + 10/5000 + 0.001 = 0, that is, 0.001 dv/dt + 0.002 + 0.001 = 0, so dv/dt = -0.003/0.001 = -3.0 V/s.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify that before switching, position P connects the 20 V source through two 5 kΩ resistors to the node containing the capacitor and the 10 kΩ–inductor branch. For t < 0 in DC steady state, open the capacitor and short the inductor; the 20 kΩ resistor is only in parallel with the ideal 20 V source and does not change the source node voltage. Compute the right node voltage by the divider/series path 5 kΩ + 5 kΩ + 10 kΩ, giving v(0-) = 10 V, and the inductor branch current i_L(0-) = 10 V/10 kΩ = 1 mA downward. By continuity, v(0+) = 10 V and i_L(0+) = 1 mA. After the switch moves to Q, the left side of the right 5 kΩ resistor is grounded. Write KCL at the capacitor top node at t = 0+: C dv/dt + v/5 kΩ + i_L = 0. Substitute C = 1 mF, v = 10 V, and i_L = 1 mA to obtain dv/dt = -3.0 V/s.

method.method_draft: First form the pre-switch DC equivalent from the image: with P closed for a long time, remove the capacitor and replace the inductor by a wire. The node voltage is found from the 20 V source feeding a 10 kΩ load through two 5 kΩ resistors, so the capacitor’s initial voltage is 10 V and the series 10 kΩ-inductor branch carries 1 mA downward. At t = 0+, use an instantaneous equivalent: represent the capacitor as a 10 V node voltage source for the purpose of finding external currents, and represent the inductor branch current as still 1 mA downward. Since Q grounds the switch arm, the right 5 kΩ resistor now draws 10 V/5 kΩ = 2 mA from the capacitor node, and the inductor branch draws another 1 mA. Thus the rest of the circuit demands 3 mA from the capacitor node, so the capacitor current in the passive downward direction is -3 mA. Divide by C = 1 mF to get dv/dt at 0+ as -3.0 V/s.

raw_record.original_question: The switch in the circuit in the figure is in position \(P\) for a long time and then moved to position \(Q\) at time \(t = 0\). The value of \(\frac{dv(t)}{dt}\) at \(t = 0^+\) is _____ V/s.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: On the left side of the circuit there is a 20 V ideal voltage source, and beside it there is a 20 kΩ resistor connected in parallel with this voltage source. The upper left is connected through a 5 kΩ resistor to the P terminal of a single-pole double-throw switch; the switch switches from P to Q at t=0. The Q terminal is connected through a vertical wire to the bottom common node. The right side of the switch is connected through another 5 kΩ resistor to the right-side node. This right-side node has a 1 mF capacitor connected in parallel to ground, and the capacitor voltage v(t) is marked as positive on top and negative on bottom; at the same time there is also a branch in which a 10 kΩ resistor and a 0.1 mH inductor are connected in series and then connected to the bottom common node.

Reasoning: When t<0, the switch has been at P for a long time, and the circuit is in DC steady state. In DC steady state, the capacitor is open-circuited and the inductor is short-circuited. The 20 kΩ resistor is only connected in parallel with the ideal 20 V source and does not change the voltage of the upper node of the power source. The right-side node is obtained by voltage division through the series path 5 kΩ + 5 kΩ + 10 kΩ: the total resistance is 20 kΩ, and the current is 20 V / 20 kΩ = 1 mA. Therefore the voltage of the right-side node, namely the voltage on the 10 kΩ, is v(0-) = 1 mA × 10 kΩ = 10 V; the inductor branch current i_L(0-) = 1 mA, with direction downward.

Since the capacitor voltage is continuous and the inductor current is continuous, v(0+) = 10 V, i_L(0+) = 1 mA downward. After t=0, the switch is connected to Q, and the left end of the right-side 5 kΩ resistor is grounded. Write KCL for the node at the top end of the capacitor at t=0+, taking the current flowing from the node to ground as positive: C dv/dt + v/5 kΩ + i_L = 0. Substitute C = 1 mF = 0.001 F, v = 10 V, i_L = 0.001 A: 0.001 dv/dt + 10/5000 + 0.001 = 0, that is, 0.001 dv/dt + 0.002 + 0.001 = 0, so dv/dt = -0.003/0.001 = -3.0 V/s.
